title: GEO glossary: AI search terms explained
description: A plain GEO glossary: 28 terms on generative engine optimisation and AI search, from citation rate and visibility score to llms.txt, E-E-A-T and drift.
lede: The words used in generative engine optimisation and AI search, defined briefly and neutrally.
answer: This GEO glossary defines the terms used in generative engine optimisation and AI search: how engines such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews build answers, how brands get cited in them, and how visibility is measured. Each definition is short and neutral, so you can use it in a brief, a board paper or a conversation with an agency.

sections.html: AI search has brought a new vocabulary with it. Some terms come from search, some from machine learning and some from how agencies like ours measure the work. Where a term describes how we measure, we say so.

items.d: Generative engine optimisation is the practice of making a brand easier for AI engines to find, trust, name and cite in their answers. It covers the pages a brand publishes, the sources engines rely on and how accurately the brand is described. The US spelling is generative engine optimization.

Answer engine optimisation is a closely related term for structuring content so that AI search features and voice assistants can lift a direct answer from it. The terms are often used interchangeably; AEO tends to focus on the format of answers, GEO on being named and cited.

A large language model is an AI model trained on large amounts of text to understand and generate language. LLMs power chat assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude, often combined with live web search.
AI Overviews are AI-generated summaries that Google shows above some search results, with links to the sources used. They are one of the 8 engines we track.
AI Mode is Google's conversational search experience, in which a user asks questions and follow-ups and receives an AI-generated answer with links instead of a standard list of results.

Retrieval-augmented generation is a method in which an AI system first retrieves relevant documents, for example through a web search, and then writes its answer from them. It is why current, readable pages can change what an engine says.
A citation is a source an AI engine links to or names as the basis for its answer. Being cited is different from being mentioned: a brand can be named without its own pages being the source.
Citation rate is the share of AI answers that cite a brand's own pages as a source. It shows whether engines rely on what the brand publishes or on third parties.
Visibility score is the share of tracked questions, across all the engines measured, where the brand appears in the answer. It is the headline measure of AI visibility in our reporting.
Share of voice is a brand's share of all brand mentions in the answers for its category, measured against the rivals the engines name.
Brand sentiment is the tone in which AI engines describe a brand, scored on every stored answer. It shows whether the brand is described positively, neutrally or with caveats.
A prompt is the question or instruction a person types into an AI engine. In GEO tracking, a prompt is one buyer question run on each engine and recorded with its answer and date.

A prompt universe is the full set of questions a brand's buyers are likely to ask AI engines. Ours is built from SEO data, the brand's own enquiries, a category map and a live engine baseline, then ranked by demand and winnability.

A question cluster is a group of closely related prompts that share one intent, such as questions comparing two neighbourhoods or two products. Work is usually planned and measured cluster by cluster.

An entity is a distinct thing, such as a company, person, product or place, that search engines and AI systems recognise and connect to facts. Clear, consistent entity data helps engines describe a brand correctly.
A knowledge graph is a database of entities and the relationships between them, used by search engines and AI systems to answer factual questions. Google's Knowledge Graph is the best-known example.
Wikidata is a free, collaboratively edited knowledge base run by the Wikimedia Foundation that stores structured facts about entities. Search engines and AI systems use it as a reference source.

Structured data, or schema markup, is code added to a web page, usually using the Schema.org vocabulary, that labels facts such as an organisation's name, a product's details or a page's questions and answers. It helps machines read the page accurately.

llms.txt is a proposed convention: a plain-text Markdown file at a website's root that points AI systems to the site's most useful pages. It is not an official standard, and support among engines varies.
E-E-A-T stands for experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trustworthiness. The term comes from Google's search quality rater guidelines and describes what Google looks for in reliable content.

Zero-click search is a search that ends without the user clicking any result, because the answer appears on the results page or in an AI summary. SparkToro and Datos (2024) found that 58.5% of US Google searches ended without a click.
Drift is when what AI engines say about a brand changes or falls out of date, often after a launch, a price change or new results. Drift alerts flag these changes so wrong facts are caught early.
The Week-1 baseline is the first full measurement of a brand's AI visibility, taken before any fixes ship. Every later result is reported against it.

A readiness scorecard rates how prepared a brand is to be named in AI answers. Ours scores 8 factors out of 10 each, for a total out of 80: brand recognition, trust and credibility, entity accuracy, technical readiness, share of answer, location authority, discovery and comparisons.

A feeder network is the set of sites and channels that send buyers and AI engines towards a brand. It includes owned channels, such as a blog, guide site, video channel, newsletter or WhatsApp channel, and earned ones, such as creators, 'best X in Y' lists and newsletters.

Rented growth comes from ads, sponsored posts and paid placements, and stops when the budget stops. Owned growth comes from assets a brand controls, such as its pages, reviews, community and channels, which keep working and compound.
Digital PR is earning coverage, mentions and links in online media, lists and publications. In GEO it matters because AI engines often draw on trusted media when they describe a brand.

A hallucination is a statement an AI model produces that sounds plausible but is false or unsupported, such as a wrong price, date or figure. Accurate, current, well-sourced pages leave fewer gaps for hallucinations to fill.

faqs.q: What is the difference between GEO and AEO?
faqs.a: They overlap and are often used interchangeably. AEO usually means formatting content so engines can lift a direct answer; GEO is broader, covering whether a brand is named, cited and described accurately in AI answers.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a mention and a citation in AI answers?
faqs.a: A mention is when the engine names the brand in its answer. A citation is when it links to or names a source as the basis for the answer. A brand can be mentioned without its own pages being cited.

faqs.q: Does llms.txt help a brand appear in AI answers?
faqs.a: llms.txt is a proposed convention, not an official standard, and support among engines varies. It can do no harm, but clear, accurate, well-structured pages and trusted third-party sources matter far more.

faqs.a: It depends on your category, starting point and the sources engines already trust. In one real-estate programme, a residential developer in India moved from a 32% to a 58% visibility score across 8 engines in under 2.5 months. That is one programme, not a promise.

faqs.q: How much does GEO cost?
faqs.a: It depends on scope: the brands, markets and questions involved. We do not publish prices. Most clients start with a Week-1 baseline, which gives a scorecard, a ranked question universe and a costed plan.

faqs.q: Do we have to sign a long contract?
faqs.a: No. There are three ways to start: a baseline and universe map; owning your strongest questions first; or a one-quarter pilot with both scoreboards reported monthly and a clear go or stop at month 3.

faqs.q: Do you guarantee rankings in ChatGPT or Google?
faqs.a: No. The engines decide what they say, and anyone who guarantees rankings is guessing. We do the work rigorously, measure from a Week-1 baseline and show every week what moved.

faqs.q: How do you measure and report results?
faqs.a: We take a Week-1 baseline, log every fix with its date and re-measure after it is published and crawled. Weekly reports compare against the baseline on two scoreboards: the AI answers, and SEO plus owned enquiries.

faqs.q: Do you name your clients or show testimonials?
faqs.a: No. We never name, describe identifiably, count or quote clients, and we show no logos or testimonials. Our case studies describe the sector and the market only.

faqs.q: Do you post on Reddit or edit Wikipedia for clients?
faqs.a: On Reddit and Quora we post openly as the brand, never through fake accounts. On Wikipedia we only propose factual corrections on talk pages, with sources, and never make promotional edits.

faqs.q: Do you write fake reviews?
faqs.a: Never. We help brands earn a steady stream of real reviews and reply to every one in public. No fabricated reviews, figures or astroturfing.

faqs.q: How do you handle compliance in India?
faqs.a: Brand, legal and regulatory sign-off comes before anything goes live. We check against RERA, ASCI and SEBI rules where they apply, and our work is aligned with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDP).

faqs.q: Can you help a listed company with what AI tells investors?
faqs.a: Yes, through our Investor Relations package. We keep AI answers accurate and current using only public disclosures, follow SEBI rules and get company sign-off before anything is published. Accuracy, not spin.

faqs.q: Are you an agency or a software tool?
faqs.a: We are an agency that runs on our own platform, Optimizer GEO. The platform tracks the engines, answers and sources; our six specialist teams ship the fixes and own the KPIs.

faqs.q: Which industries do you work in?
faqs.a: Nine: real estate and hospitality; financial services and investor relations; retail and consumer brands; food and FMCG; B2B and professional services; technology and SaaS; pharma and healthcare; manufacturing; industrial and engineering; cinema and entertainment.

faqs.q: Which countries do you work in?
faqs.a: Our home market is India. We also work in the United States and Mauritius.

faqs.q: What do we get in the first week?
faqs.a: A Week-1 baseline: a readiness scorecard across 8 factors, a ranked universe of the questions your buyers ask, and a costed plan. It is the line every later result is measured against.

faqs.q: How do we get started?
faqs.a: Email abhay@optimizer360.ai or request an AI audit on our contact page. It shows which engines name you, who they name instead, the sources they cite and the first fixes we would make.

title: Privacy notice for this website
description: Our privacy notice: no analytics or advertising cookies, forms that open your own email app, and your rights under India's DPDP Act 2023 and other laws.
lede: Last updated: 10 November 2026. What this website collects, what it does not, and how to reach us about your data.
answer: This website does not use analytics or advertising cookies. It stores one setting, your colour-mode preference, in your browser's localStorage. The contact and audit forms do not send data to a server: they open your own email app with a prefilled message to abhay@optimizer360.ai. We use the emails we receive only to reply, never sell them, and keep them only as long as needed.

sections.html:
This notice covers the website optimizer360.ai, run by Optimizer360. Where we receive personal data from you, we decide how it is used, which under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 makes us the data fiduciary.

Last updated: 10 November 2026.

• No analytics or advertising cookies. We do not use them.
  • Your colour-mode preference. If you switch between light and dark mode, the choice is saved in your browser's localStorage so the site remembers it. It stays on your device and is not sent to us. You can clear it at any time in your browser settings.
  • Standard technical data. Like any website, the servers that deliver these pages may record basic technical information, such as IP address, browser type and the page requested, to keep the site secure and running. We do not use it to profile visitors.

sections.h2: How do the contact and audit forms work?
sections.html: The forms on this site do not submit anything to a server. When you press the button, your own email app opens with a message to abhay@optimizer360.ai, filled in with what you typed. Nothing reaches us unless you choose to send that email. Your email provider handles the message under its own privacy terms.

sections.h2: What happens to emails you send us?
sections.html:
• We use them to reply to you and to carry on the conversation you started.
  • We do not sell them, and we do not use them for advertising.
  • We keep them only as long as we need them for that conversation and any work that follows, or as long as the law requires.

sections.h2: What are your rights under India's DPDP Act 2023?
sections.html:
Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 you have the right to:

  • Access: ask what personal data we hold about you and how we use it.
  • Correction: ask us to correct, complete or update it.
  • Erasure: ask us to delete it, unless the law requires us to keep it.
  • Grievance redressal: raise a complaint with us. If you are not satisfied with our response, you may approach the Data Protection Board of India.
  • Nomination: name someone to exercise these rights for you in the event of death or incapacity.

To use any of these rights, email abhay@optimizer360.ai.

sections.h2: Visitors from the EU, UK and US
sections.html:
EU and UK: if the GDPR or UK GDPR applies to you, you have rights to access, correct, erase, restrict, object to and move your personal data, and to complain to your local data protection authority. We process the emails you send us to reply to your request.

United States: we do not sell or share your personal information, and we do not use it for targeted advertising. You can ask us to tell you what we hold or to delete it.

sections.h2: How do I contact you about privacy?
sections.html: Email abhay@optimizer360.ai with "Privacy" in the subject line.
If we add analytics or a form backend, this notice will be updated first.

faqs.q: Does the Optimizer360 website use cookies?
faqs.a: No analytics or advertising cookies. The only thing stored is your colour-mode preference, kept in your browser's localStorage on your own device.

faqs.a: No. It opens your own email app with a prefilled message to abhay@optimizer360.ai. Nothing reaches us unless you choose to send that email.
